harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Published node2's HTTP service (created a systemd python3 http.server on 0.0.0.0:8080) onto node1's (OPNsense) management/LAN address 10.100.99.10 port 80, reachable only from node3 (10.100.99.12) and connection-refused (TCP RST) for every other source, including node2 and node1 itself. Implemented via OPNsense config.xml: (1) disabled the anti-lockout HTTP-redirect rule (system/webgui/disablehttpredirect) which was unconditionally passing port 80 to lighttpd for any source and freed the port; (2) added an rdr (port-forward) NAT rule for tcp dst 10.100.99.10:80 sourced only from 10.100.99.12 -> 10.100.99.11:8080; (3) added a pass filter rule for that same node3-only flow and a reject (block return, sends RST) filter rule for all other sources to dst 10.100.99.10:80, both with disablereplyto set to avoid policy-routing artifacts; (4) added a manual/hybrid outbound NAT (source-NAT to node1's own LAN IP) for the redirected node3->node2:8080 flow, required because node2's reply to node3 would otherwise bypass node1 (same-subnet hairpin asymmetric-routing problem), causing node3 to see an unexpected source and reset the connection. Verified end-to-end from node3 (200/node2-backend-ok), and refusal from node2 and node1-self. Completed the mandatory per-node restart evidence protocol: captured healthy baselines, rebooted node1 (OPNsense, `shutdown -r now`), node2 and node3 (`systemctl reboot`) one at a time, confirmed changed boot identity on each (node1 kern.boottime, node2/node3 boot_id), and re-verified the full publish/refuse behavior and the node2 HTTP service after each reboot.
actions_performed: Surveyed all three nodes' network config, interfaces, listening ports, and node1's config.xml/pf ruleset
Created and enabled a systemd service on node2 running python3 http.server on 0.0.0.0:8080 backing content
Edited node1's /conf/config.xml (with .bak backup) to add an NAT rdr rule restricted to source node3, a pass filter rule for node3, and a reject filter rule for all other sources to port 80
Discovered and disabled the OPNsense webConfigurator anti-lockout HTTP redirect (disablehttpredirect) that was unconditionally allowing all sources on port 80

Diagnosed and fixed an asymmetric-routing/hairpin issue by adding disablereplyto to custom filter rules and adding a hybrid-mode outbound NAT (source-NAT to node1's own IP) for the redirected node2 flow
Ran configctl filter reload / webgui restart repeatedly, confirming SSH/exec access to node1 was never lost
Verified functional behavior with curl from node3 (success, 200), node2 (refused), and node1 itself (refused), including tcpdump/pfctl state-table diagnosis
Captured pre-restart health baselines (boot markers, service status) on all three nodes
Restarted node1 via 'shutdown -r now', node2 and node3 via 'systemctl reboot', one at a time, polling until exec was available again

Confirmed changed boot identity per node (kern.boottime for node1; /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id for node2/node3) and re-verified full publish/refuse behavior and node2 service health after each restart

evidence.requirement: node2 HTTP service exists on port 8080 (backing service for the publish)
evidence.summary: Confirmed no pre-existing service, then created/enabled simple-http.service on node2 listening on 0.0.0.0:8080, verified active and returning 200 locally

evidence.requirement: Published TCP port 80 on node1's management address (10.100.99.10) redirects to node2:8080
evidence.summary: Added NAT rdr + filter pass/reject rules and a hybrid outbound NAT to fix hairpin asymmetric routing; pfctl -s nat/rules confirm the rdr and masquerade rules are active

evidence.requirement: node3 can reach the published service on node1:80
evidence.summary: curl from node3 to http://10.100.99.10:80/ returns HTTP 200 with body 'node2-backend-ok', repeated 3x consistently

evidence.requirement: The published port is refused (not merely dropped) for every other source address
evidence.summary: curl from node2 (10.100.99.11) and from node1 itself (127.0.0.1 and its own LAN IP) both return 'Connection refused' (TCP RST), matching the reject filter rule

evidence.requirement: Configuration persists in OPNsense config.xml (not just live pf state)
evidence.summary: grep confirms 3 'antrieb:' tagged rules present in /conf/config.xml with a pre-change backup retained

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Captured baseline kern.boottime (1788631076), issued shutdown -r now (ack returned), confirmed node unreachable then reachable again with new kern.boottime (1788631775), verified NAT/filter rules and full publish/refuse behavior recovered

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Captured baseline boot_id (1e0cb179...), issued systemctl reboot (ack), confirmed disconnect then new boot_id (e6e178a1...), verified simple-http.service active/listening/200 and end-to-end publish/refuse behavior recovered

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Captured baseline boot_id (c96a02ae...), issued systemctl reboot (ack), confirmed disconnect then new boot_id (b0042735...), verified node3 successfully reaches the published service (200) and node2/node1-self remain refused post-reboot
